thread:
jamie: heads up — saw a small spike of reconnects + double charge traces for WS sessions in eu-west1 between 03:10–03:16 UTC. looks correlated with resume fallback hitting route B after a route swap.
neha: any console links or query IDs?
jamie: yes, dashboard -> Streaming > Route Health shows route_bounce_count up x3. example trace id: trace-0a1b2c. logs: `proxy: resume_attempt=1 route=alpha -> beta auth_ok=true billing_token=tn_42` then a second resume that increments charge.
sam: is this the resume idempotency bug we patched last month? sounds like resume tokens got lost on the proxy handoff.
lee: could be sticky routing TTL. if the proxy hands off mid-resume the new route treats it as fresh and bills.
neha: console-bot: can you surface a link to the specific spike? :point_down:
console-bot: https://console.redwood.ai/streams/route_health?range=03:00-03:30&filter=route_bounce_count%3E0 (attached sample graph)
jamie: thanks. attaching a short snippet from the proxy logs: ```
[03:12:01] conn=abcd resume_id=rz123 route=alpha accepted
[03:12:02] proxy-handoff conn=abcd new_route=beta
[03:12:03] conn=abcd resume_id=rz123 route=beta accepted billing: incremented
```
sam: hmm that sequence implies resume is not being validated against an opaque lease. we should either treat resume as idempotent across routes or require resume->stickiness until handshake completes.
lee: routing-policy-wise we have a 10s grace window that lets route claim expire early. maybe too short during handoffs under load.
neha: proposal: increase grace window to 30s for canary and add a resume-claim header so proxies can reconcile. also surface resume vs reconnect counts on console (different metric names).
jamie: agreed. console UX: current metric `reconnects` conflates both reconnect and resume. that's why product saw spike and assumed client flakiness. split would help.
sam: telemetry ask: add trace_id and route_before/route_after to the resume_event so we can dedupe billing increments when route changes within the same resume_id. small patch in proxy + ingestion.
lee: how invasive is that? we need to keep payload size small. maybe encode route pair as `rb:alpha->beta` in the event.
neha: ops-bot: create canary feature flag `resume-sticky-grace-30s` in eu-west1 for next deploy and bind to traffic sample 5%.
ops-bot: canary flag created: resume-sticky-grace-30s. rollout window scheduled 2h from now. owner: sam.
sam: i'll open a tiny PR for the telemetry name changes + route_pair field. test plan: unit test + deploy to staging, run the resume replay harness (we have a replay that reproduces handoff) and assert single billing increment per resume_id across routes.
jamie: also add a console annotation for the canary so support sees it in Alerts.
neha: UX note — show a small tooltip explaining "resume (idempotent reconnect) vs reconnect (fresh session)" so non-eng folks don't misinterpret.
lee: we should also add an aggregator rule in billing pipeline that dedups events with same resume_id within 60s unless explicit new_session=true. low-risk safety net.
sam: agreed. i'll include that in the PR but gate it behind the canary flag.
jamie: timeline?
sam: PR by EOD, staging verification tomorrow morning, canary start in 2h (ops-bot already scheduled), full rollout after 24h if metrics look good.
neha: i'll update the console dashboard rows: split `streams.reconnects` -> `streams.resume_events`, `streams.fresh_reconnects`. i'll add the tooltip and the trace drilldown link.
lee: quick question — what alert thresholds? current alert fires when total reconnects > 200/min. with split we should set resume threshold higher because resume is expected for flaky mobile networks. maybe set fresh_reconnects > 50/min and resume_events > 500/min? open to tuning after baseline.
jamie: sounds reasonable. also add an ops-runbook note to check route_bounce_count and correlate with billing diffs.
ops-bot: alert created: fresh_reconnects_high -> notify #eng-oncall, #support.
sam: thanks. i'll post PR link here when ready.
jamie: appreciated. small followup: can we also log client-side resume attempts count to detect client replay loops?
neha: good call — add client_resume_attempts meta but mark as opt-in sampling (1%). don't want to blow up storage.
lee: ok let's reconvene if the canary spikes billing again. otherwise we'll proceed with full rollout. :thumbsup:
sam: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/s/1234 (draft)
jamie: closing loop — flagged support to hold off any customer-facing comms until we confirm root cause. thanks everyone.
summary: Spike in WS resume-related reconnects caused double billing when route handoff happened mid-resume; plan: canary increase grace window, split console metrics for resume vs reconnect, add route_pair telemetry and billing dedupe, rollout + runbook updates.
